types.name: Generator
types.doc: A generator is a stackless coroutine that can `yield` values back to the dispatcher. For an isolated execution context, consider using threads.

types.name: Fiber
types.doc: A fiber is a stackful coroutine: a function call that runs on its own stack and can be suspended at any call depth with `suspend`. It is created with `fiber f(args)` and advanced with `resume`. A fiber carries no value. Use a generator to produce values.

methods.name: cancel
methods.doc: Ends a fiber that is not done without running the rest of its function. Every call that the fiber is in returns at once, from the innermost one out, and the values that the calls own are destructed as at a `return`. A fiber that was never resumed is ended without the call and its arguments are released. Returns whether the fiber is done afterwards. A fiber that is running is not cancelled, and neither is one that is suspended inside the `@deinit` of a `^T` reference.

methods.name: resume
methods.doc: Runs the fiber until it suspends or its function returns. Returns `.suspended` or `.done`. Resuming a fiber that is done returns `.done`.

methods.name: waiting
methods.doc: Whether the fiber is suspended at an `await` or a `Future.wait_any` whose future is not done. A `resume` of such a fiber returns `.suspended` at once.

funcs.name: wait_ready
funcs.doc: Waits until a future that a suspended fiber of this thread awaits is done, and returns `true`. Returns `false` at once when no fiber awaits a future. A scheduler loop calls it when a round of `resume` calls made no progress. Futures of spawned threads are waited for like `await` does. When only the host can complete the futures, the eval is suspended and all of them are pending (see `cl_vm_pending_futures`). Inside a fiber, that fiber is suspended until one of the futures is done.

types.name: Scope
types.doc: A group of fibers that do not outlive it. `start` adds a fiber and `join` runs the fibers until all of them are done. A scope that is destructed joins its fibers first, so a fiber of a scope never runs after the block that holds the scope. The entry function of a fiber returns `void` or `!void`. `join` returns the first error that a fiber returned. After an error the other fibers are cancelled (`Fiber.cancel`): they do not run on.

methods.name: start
methods.doc: Adds a fiber that calls `func(args)`. The arguments are evaluated now. The fiber starts in `join`.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The number of fibers that are not done.

methods.name: join
methods.doc: Runs the fibers until all of them are done. A fiber that stops at `suspend` gives the others a turn. When every fiber waits for a future, the scope waits like `Fiber.wait_ready`. Returns the first error that a fiber returned. More fibers can be started after a `join`.

methods.name: abort
methods.doc: Cancels the fibers that are not done (`Fiber.cancel`) and drops an error that a fiber returned. A fiber that can not be cancelled runs to its end first.

funcs.name: new_slice_buffer
funcs.doc: A `Slice` buffer holds the number of initialized elements in its first 8 bytes, then the elements. Slices that share a buffer can have different lengths, so `Slice.@deinit` destructs this count instead of its own length. Ops that resize keep it equal to the result's length. The result of `clone_on_resize` is never a sub-slice, so its count is `(as[Ptr[int]] ptr)[-1]` (no call, hot path). Only managed element types read the count, so the resize ops skip it for the others.

funcs.name: hypot

funcs.name: isInt
funcs.doc: Returns true if the float has no fractional part, otherwise false.

funcs.name: isNaN
funcs.doc: Returns whether x is not a number.

funcs.name: ln
funcs.doc: Returns the natural logarithm (㏒e; also, ㏑) of x.

funcs.name: log
funcs.doc: Returns the logarithm of y with base x.

funcs.name: log10
funcs.doc: Returns the base-10 logarithm of x.

funcs.name: log1p
funcs.doc: Returns the natural logarithm (㏒e; also ㏑) of 1 + x for the number x.

funcs.name: log2
funcs.doc: Returns the base-2 logarithm of x.

funcs.name: max

funcs.name: min
funcs.doc: Returns the smallest of two numbers.

funcs.name: mul32

funcs.name: pow
funcs.doc: Returns base x to the exponent power y (that is, x^y).

funcs.name: random
funcs.doc: Returns a pseudo-random number between 0 and 1.

funcs.name: round
funcs.doc: Returns the value of the number x rounded to the nearest integer.

funcs.name: sign

funcs.name: sin
funcs.doc: Returns the sine of x.

funcs.name: sinh
funcs.doc: Returns the hyperbolic sine of x.

funcs.name: sqrt
funcs.doc: Returns the positive square root of x.

funcs.name: tan
funcs.doc: Returns the tangent of x.

funcs.name: tanh
funcs.doc: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.

funcs.name: trunc
funcs.doc: Returns the integer portion of x, removing any fractional digits.

funcs.name: stderr

funcs.name: stdin

funcs.name: stdout

funcs.name: args

funcs.name: dirname

funcs.name: exit

funcs.name: fetchUrl

funcs.doc: Returns all environment variables as a map.

funcs.name: nanoTime

funcs.name: open_file
